newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court extends Rao's bail in forgery case.
newsitem.headline: Indian court extends Rao's bail in forgery case.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao on Monday won a three-week extension of bail in a criminal forgery case, a lawyer representing the embattled politician said.
R.K. Anand said chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar extended the temporary bail granted to Rao last week until November 6 -- one week after a hearing in the case.

The judge's decision was another small victory for Rao in the tangled legal proceedings which have clouded the 75-year-old politician's future and created tension between his Congress party and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government.
Rao was due to become the first former prime minister to appear in court in a criminal case.

But two cases -- one involving alleged forgery, the other criminal conspiracy to cheat -- have become bogged down in procedural manoeuvres, and Rao has been spared the humiliation of either a court appearance or being taken into custody.
In the forgery case involving an alleged attempt to defame a politician in 1989, the judge postponed the hearing until October 30, and granted the extension of temporary bail until November 6.
Anand has asked another judge to grant Rao pre-emptive, or anticipatory, bail in the cheating case. Rao denies accusations he conspired to cheat a businessman of $100,000 in 1983.

A hearing in the case was set for Wednesday. But Rao has been exempted from having to appear until the Delhi High Court responds to a Supreme Court ruling ordering any trials involving him to be shifted from crowded local courts to a safer location.
Authorities were expected to propose a substitute venue on Monday. Court authorities said they expected Wednesday's hearing to be postponed until later this month.
Rao's lawyers convinced the Supreme Court last week that their client could be attacked by militant extremists if he appeared in the teeming local courts.
Delhi police argued that they could not guard against threats by Kashmiri, Sikh and Moslem extremists, and that any trial involving Rao should be held in a less accessible spot.
Rao is among four former prime ministers who are guarded night and day by crack commandos carrying machine guns.

Given the time it will take to set up a special trial venue and the fact the courts will close for several days for the Hindu holiday Dusshera next Monday, Rao was not expected to appear in court until later this month, legal experts said.
Rao stepped down as Congress party chief last month after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in the cheating case.

Rao had pledged his party's backing to Deve Gowda's centre-left minority coalition. But his successor, Sitaram Kesri, has threatened to withdraw the backing unless Deve Gowda backs a Congress alliance in Uttar Pradesh state.
